Example_Context: In a detailed accrual dataset Cat can be the economic accrual category; confirm from neighbouring liability and amount fields.
In a site reference or mapping dataset Cat can describe the location/site type rather than a financial category.
In a tax or other-liability support schedule Cat can be a liability/control classification; use worksheet and neighbouring-field context.
Map1 may be a legacy management OCL subclass or reporting classification and must not be universalized across engagements.
Description beside Nominal/account fields normally describes the GL account rather than a vendor or accrual obligation.
Liability Description beside site/liability code/category/month/value describes the operational accrual line.
Description in an employee-liability schedule describes the employee-liability item and is not automatically an account description.
Entity is an organizational/legal-entity identifier when supported by the dataset grain.
Nominal is commonly the GL/nominal account code when paired with an account description and balances.
Closing Balance is the point-in-time liability balance for the applicable period/entity/grain.
Prior Year is a comparative balance and should not be treated as a current-period transaction amount.
Movement is the change between supported comparative balances and should preserve the source sign convention.
Month represents the accounting period when paired with a balance/value measure.
Value is the financial amount when the surrounding grain identifies site/liability/month.
Category in an explicit account-mapping schedule is a mapping target supported by the mapping context.
Parent Category is the higher-level mapping/hierarchy field when explicitly supplied by the source.

Dataset_Context: Project accrual or project master dataset
Example_Context: Project ID is a project-level identifier useful for linking accruals/AP/contracts/project status when evidence supports the relationship.

Dataset_Context: Project accrual AP or contract-obligation dataset
Example_Context: Contract ID is a contract identifier useful for corroborating obligations and possible duplicate/completeness testing.

Dataset_Context: Project accrual AP or contract-obligation dataset
Example_Context: PO is a purchase-order identifier and can support cross-dataset linkage when cardinality is validated.
Opening is the opening accrual balance in a roll-forward and should reconcile to prior closing where supported.
Additions is the amount newly accrued during the period under the source sign convention.
Utilisation is settlement/use of an existing accrual and should not be conflated with additions.
Release is a release/reversal of an accrual and may be relevant to QoE when linked to P&L evidence.
Reclass is a reclassification/other roll-forward movement and should preserve source sign and meaning.
Closing is the roll-forward closing balance and should reconcile to the corresponding closing balance where supported.
Accrual Date is evidence for true aging when it represents the actual booking/obligation date and is validated in context.
Expected Settlement Date is a settlement expectation field and can support settlement/aging analysis without proving actual payment.
Service Period Start identifies the beginning of the economic service period and can support cutoff/completeness analysis.
Service Period End identifies the end of the economic service period and can support cutoff/completeness analysis.
Certified Work is evidence of work performed/certified and can support adequacy/completeness testing when linked to the obligation.
Estimated Unbilled Amount is an estimate of incurred but uninvoiced obligation and should be corroborated rather than treated as booked accrual automatically.
Amount Invoiced is invoiced obligation evidence and can support adequacy/settlement tests when linked appropriately.

Example_Context: Payment Date is actual settlement timing evidence and can support subsequent-payment testing.
